question: Do contiguous whole-turn commitments to the validated three-turn teacher transfer complete-game benefit that one isolated teacher turn did not, and how do they compare with a dispersed 25-percent teacher-turn mixture?
arena: Classic Generic procedural_v2 11x9, two players, 2400-action finite horizon with material adjudication flagged nonterminal
opponent: Frozen routed-v6 direct policy on every opponent turn
candidate_implementation: Choose a frozen policy once at each candidate-seat turn start and let it control the complete turn. The first-k arms use exact native three-turn search for root turn indices 0 through k-1, then frozen direct for the rest. distributed_25 uses the existing deterministic seed/seat/turn hash; full_teacher uses exact native search on every candidate turn. Never splice atomic teacher actions into direct turns.
analysis: Record actual teacher/root turns, game length, terminal and action-limit-adjudicated outcomes by root seat. Compare each arm against direct on the same map and both seats, grouping by independent map; separately compare first_2, first_4 and first_8 against first_1. Report exact two-sided map sign tests descriptively, with all seven arms and any censoring visible. Compare first_4 versus distributed_25 as an exploratory schedule contrast only after showing actual teacher-turn counts, not as an equal-budget causal estimate.
decision_rule: This is a mechanism experiment, not a student promotion gate. If multi-turn blocks improve complete-game outcomes while first_1 does not, pursue a new temporally coherent outcome-grounded distillation target on disjoint fit/calibration/validation/game windows. If not, reject the contiguous-block explanation and inspect state-dependent teacher use. Do not train or deploy from this diagnostic.
resources: Run heavy games only on SSH server fedora-toolbox, one pinned CPU nice19, Rayon/BLAS capped, 1800-second hard timeout, tiny JSON, no GPU or preemption. Never touch the remote original repo.
